Subject: Pilot budget & PO question

Jonas / team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — super helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our end as we scope next steps for a November pilot:  

- Expected token profile: roughly 80–150M tokens/month (spiky peak windows ~3–4M/day).
- Target unit economics we discussed: our CFO is looking for a working target of ~$650 / 1M tokens (including embeddings & generation mix).
- Procurement gating: procurement only issues POs above $20k/month; anything under that they can approve on a credit card or short-term contract. If we commit to a 6–12 month reserved band, they may consider a single PO for the first quarter.

Can you confirm what price bands / PO thresholds Redwood typically sees for pilots of this size, and whether there are discounted unit rates at commit levels (e.g., 200M+ tokens / month)? Also: can you share a short pricing sheet we can give to procurement?

Appreciate it — Samir
EdgeMap

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot budget & PO question

Samir — thanks for the summary and the token profile. Quick answers up front, then attaching a concise pricing sheet.

1) Unit economics: for the profile you shared (80–150M/mo mixed workload) a practical target is $500–$850 / 1M tokens depending on model selection, batching/latency SLO, and whether you take a reserved/dedicated pool. At ~200M tokens/month we can layer a commit discount that pushes toward the low end of that range.

2) PO/Procurement: Redwood’s common procurement path is:
  - < $10k/month: CC or short-term contract (fast)
  - $10k–$50k/month: PO accepted; standard SOW + 30–45 day legal review
  - > $50k/month: PO + enterprise contract; legal and security review (SOC2 artifacts) often required

3) Pilots: customers typically choose a 3-month pilot with either a monthly usage commit or a small reserved pool. We can structure a pilot with a soft commit and a conversion credit if you move to a longer reserved contract.

I’ve attached: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf (rows: model, latency tier, $/1M tokens) and a short pilot MOP template that spells procurement asks.

Next steps I propose:
- Monica to map pricing bands to your token mix and produce 2 commit scenarios: (A) conservative 80M/mo; (B) aggressive 150M/mo.
- Internal: confirm whether a PO at $25k/month would be fast enough for you to start in Q4.

If that looks good, Monica and I can join procurement call next week.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf, pilot-scope-mop-template.xlsx

Samir / Priya — I ran the token mix scenarios and included model / latency assumptions inline:  

Scenario A — conservative (80M/mo)- Model mix: 70% embeddings, 30% generation; latency tier: standard- Estimated list unit price (no commit): $980 / 1M tokens- Estimated discounted unit price with a 3mo reserved commit (80M/month): $740 / 1M tokens- Total monthly run-rate (list): ~$78k; with reserved discount: ~$59k

Scenario B — aggressive (150M/mo)- Model mix: 50/50; latency tier: standard-to-fast- Estimated list unit price (no commit): $920 / 1M tokens- Discounted unit price with a 3mo reserved commit (150M/month): $610 / 1M tokens- Total monthly run-rate (list): ~$138k; with reserved discount: ~$92k

Notes and procurement gating observations:
- If procurement only issues POs >$20k/month, both scenarios push you into PO territory. We can structure the pilot as either a CC-backed first month + PO for months 2–3, or a 3mo PO with a single invoice if your legal is comfortable.
- If you need to stay below $50k to avoid deeper legal review, we can craft a narrower pilot (~60–75M/month) or pursue a stepped commit that starts lower and scales.

Ask: can you confirm which procurement band you need to hit to avoid multi-week legal review (Samir: you mentioned $20k as the threshold — is that the correct internal gate?), and whether HorizonML (Priya) is also ok with a single PO covering Q4 initial months?

Thanks — Monica
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — this is helpful and a bit higher than our target but useful for procurement context. A few clarifications:  

- The $20k gate I mentioned is the threshold for an expedited PO; anything above $20k triggers procurement to request at least a basic SOW and a 2–3 week review. Anything above $50k kicks it to Vendor Risk and Legal.
- CFO would prefer us to land at or under $50k/month for the pilot to avoid the longer enterprise review, but if the pilot helps de-risk a larger commit they can sign off on a one-off exception.

Action: please send a narrow pilot option that stays <= $50k/month while still showing meaningful coverage (ideally a 75M/mo plan). If that can be shown to scale to 150M/mo with the commit discount called out, we can present to procurement next week.

Samir
